il_k_public_enemy_area.blurb: A bouldering zone within the Holy Boulders, the sandstone problem field in the forested hills of southern Illinois. Public Enemy is one of the larger clusters there, with a few dozen problems on grippy, well-featured stone. Most of what is here sits between V1 and V3, so there is plenty for newer boulderers, and a handful of hard lines reach up to V10; Son of the Morning (V8), Fading Light (V7) and Platypus (V8) are among the stronger ones, while Anthrax Arête (V2) is a fine easier line. Cool weather is the comfortable window, roughly autumn through early spring; summer brings heat, humidity, ticks and thick vegetation. Bring pads and expect a walk through the woods.
il_k_public_enemy_area.parking_note: Two small lots sit west of the boulders along Macedonia Road, on national forest land. Park there and walk in on foot.

ks_lake_olathe.blurb: A small lakeside cluster of boulders in a city park in Olathe, in the Kansas City area. The stone is limestone in blocks roughly 10 to 14 feet tall, and many problems are on overhanging faces and short roofs, so expect steep, powerful moves rather than tall lines. The rock can be crumbly, so test holds before committing. Grades run from V0 to V8 with the bulk between V0 and V3, which makes it a friendly spot for newer boulderers; Skink Hole (V7-8) is the hard standout, while Cave Spider (V3) and Elytra (V3) are popular. The problems are spread over a few sections around the water, including a point, a lakeside block, a small cave and a main overhang. Bring pads.
ks_lake_olathe.parking_note: Leave the car at the shelter beside the nature playground, then head toward the end of the loop road where the trail starts.
ks_lake_olathe.approach: From the playground end of the loop road, take the trail south and bear right at the first fork. When boulder tops appear on your right, a small stone path leads beneath the overhang. If you reach a concrete circle you have overshot.

ks_rock_city.blurb: A field of rounded sandstone concretions in a small park outside Minneapolis, in north-central Kansas. The spheres were cemented harder than the surrounding sand, so they now stand alone as free boulders, the bigger ones around 15 to 20 feet across. It is bouldering only, and the climbing is mostly easy to moderate: nearly everything is between V0 and V4, with just a couple of harder outliers. Assent (V1), Hoop Snake Traverse (V4) and Daddy's Home (V4) are among the favorites. The stone is solid with rounded holds, and lichen or plants on some of them are normally not a problem. The formations are unusual enough to be worth a visit on their own, and the low grades suit families and newer climbers.

ky_bouldering_area.blurb: A small bouldering zone tucked beneath the Muscle Beach cliff in the Northern Gorge of the Red River Gorge. A low rock ridge links the pinnacle called Minas Ithil to the main ridge, and the sandstone blocks sit along a short cliffline on its south-facing side, with a few free-standing boulders and a satellite group down the slope. This is the gentle end of the gorge's bouldering: problems run from V0 to V2, mostly V0 and V1, which suits beginners, warm-ups and kids. The walk in crosses a creek and climbs a hillside, and the nearby main cliff, famous for offwidths, tends to see few visitors, so the area is often quiet.

ky_military_wall.blurb: One of the taller walls in the Northern Gorge, a short uphill hike from the Martin's Fork trailhead. The sandstone is full of big pockets, patterned bands of iron-rich rock and a lot of overhanging ground, which makes for pumpy sport climbing with pinches, sidepulls and knee bars. Grades center on 5.11 and 5.12, with a good spread of 5.10s, some harder lines above that, a few easier vertical routes to warm up on, and a number of trad lines. Fuzzy Undercling (5.11b), Gung Ho (5.12b) and Tissue Tiger (5.12b) are among the favorites. The wall catches sun until about early afternoon, steeper lines tend to stay dry in rain, and some starts are polished enough to feel harder than their grade.

ky_the_venue.blurb: A big, steep cave crag in the Wilson Hollow section of Cave Fork Recreational Preserve, one of the newer developments in the Red River Gorge. The cave steepens toward its middle, with shorter vertical walls at either end, so the routes lean toward sustained sequences and distinct hard moves rather than straight pocket-pulling. Grades start in the 5.8 to 5.11 range on the flanks, but the weight of the crag is in 5.12 and 5.13, with a good number of 5.14s for the strongest. Bring a 70 m rope for the tallest lines. Since the wall curves, sun reaches different sections at different hours: the left side gets morning light and the far right gets late afternoon. The walk in is about a mile.
ky_the_venue.approach: Go through the gate on the road from the parking area, follow the wide flat track over a few small bridges and a marshy stretch, then bear right on a dirt road until a cliff trail forks off to the right. That trail reaches the right side of the cave; to reach the left side, come from the neighboring crags instead.

ky_infirmary_the.blurb: One of the best-known crags in Miller Fork Recreational Preserve, a steep wall and cove in the Red River Gorge. It is almost all sport climbing with a few trad lines, and the routes are mainly overhanging and sustained at 5.11 and 5.12, with a scattering of 5.13s and a set of easier lines on the edges. Last Rites (5.12b), Plague Doctor (5.12a) and Magic Bed (5.11b/c) are among the highlights, and the route names follow a hospital theme. The preserve is reached by a rough gravel road that suits high-clearance vehicles, and the shared lot can fill on busy days. From the lot the walk crosses the river, follows the road uphill and branches onto a trail beside a stream.
ky_infirmary_the.parking_note: Use the large gravel lot at the preserve trailhead. The way in is a rough gravel road, reached from KY-11 by Shoemaker Ridge Road and then Hell Creek Road, so a high-clearance or four-wheel-drive vehicle is best. Park close against neighboring cars.
ky_infirmary_the.approach: Cross the river from the lot and follow the road uphill. Take the second road on the left (signed for Serenity Point), pass the Serenity Point and Deep End trail turnoffs, cross a stream, and the crag trail is on the right.
